rows.title_full: AN ACT REMOVING CARDBOARD WASTAGE IN THE PRODUCTION PROCESS OF CONSUMER PRODUCTS
rows.abstract:
Seeks to do away with outer box packaging that are unnecessary and maintained mostly for aesthetics; and those goods which do not require outer protective covers and those which can be safely sold to consumers without the boxes shall be covered by this law.

Provides for the development of \"National Waste Reduction Program\" which mandates the D E N R and the   
D T I to create plans and guidelines for manufacturing companies to reduce waste such as cardboard boxes
in the packaging and distribution of consumer products.

rows.author: I105
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO REGULATE THE FARE RATES OF TRANSPORT NETWORK COMPANIES AND TRANSPORTATION NETWORK VEHICLES SERVICE
rows.abstract:
Provides that T N Cs and T N V S be subject for the full regulation and supervision by the L T F R B, specifically in the standardization of fare rates, system of refund in case of overcharging and adjustments of such standardized fare rates.

States that fare rates for T N V S shall be determined and adjusted by the L T F R B taking into consideration the: a) make/type of the vehicle; b) year model; c) time of service; and d) distance covered.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE FULL AND EFFECTIVE IMPLEMENTATION AND ENFORCEMENT OF INTERNATIONAL MARITIME INSTRUMENTS OF WHICH THE PHILIPPINES IS A STATE PARTY
rows.abstract:
Refers \"International Maritime Instruments\" to all conventions, codes recommendations, procedures, guidelines, or other similar instruments pertaining to safety of life at sea, prevention of pollution from ships, load lines, tonnage measurements of ships, and regulations for preventing collisions at sea, of which the Philippines is a State Party, including International Conventions as provided in this Act.

Enumerates the powers and functions of the DOTr and the PCG; Mandates MARINA to recommend to the DFA the adoption of international maritime instruments which the Phils. is not yet a party, so that the appropriate recommendation can be made; and that in the case of any subsequent amendment to any technical annex of any existing international convention or treaty to which the Phils. is already a party and which is deemed accepted by the State Parties to the convention after the lapse of the specified time, the MARINA is empowered and authorized to amend and revise its rules and regulations to conform with the amendments to the relevant convention or treaty.

Provides for coordination among regulatory agencies as follows: Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) under the DOST, and the National Mapping and Resource Information Authority (NAMRIA) under the DENR, among others.
rows.alias_name: \"Maritime Safety, Security and Prevention of Ship-Sourced Pollution Act of the Philippines\"

rows.author: F123
rows.title_full: AN ACT MANDATING ALL BARANGAYS TO CREATE A REGISTRY OF SKILLED WORKERS
rows.title_short: Mandating All Barangays To Create A Registry Of Skilled Workers
rows.abstract:
Mandates all barangays to create and make public a registry that will serve as a database for all skilled workers who are willing to make their services available in the locality.

Prohibits the barangay to collect fees for the inclusion of a skilled worker´s name and corresponding details in the registry. However, if the barangay decides to issue an ID pertaining to the skilled worker and the latter agrees to avail one, the barangay may collect a reasonable fee that would cover the cost of the production of the ID.

rows.author: J095
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING MENTAL HEALTH WELLNESS LEAVE TO ALL EMPLOYEES IN THE PRIVATE SECTOR
rows.abstract:
Aims to address the steadily declining mental health and wellness needs of the modern workforce and the increase incidence of suicide and mental disorders due to either lack of access to professional help or the stigma that still exists in society against those who seek help for their mental health issues.

States that all employees of the private sector are entitled to mental health wellness leaves for five (5) days with full pay per annum and provides that unused leaves shall not be carried over to the next year nor it can be monetized.

Mandates employers to offer and implement programs to raise awareness on mental health and to ensure their employees' mental wellbeing.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2020-02-17

rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING ADDITIONAL BENEFITS TO PROSECUTORS OF THE NATIONAL PROSECUTION SERVICE, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 10071, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE \"PROSECUTION SERVICE ACT OF 2010\"
rows.abstract:
Aims to properly compensate the prosecutors due to the great risks and perils they encounter and the threat and imminent danger they face due to the nature of their profession.

Seeks to grant them additional benefits: by providing a monthly hazard pay during their incumbency in an amount equivalent to 25% of their basic salary; the issuance of service firearms for their protection against death threats as a consequence of the performance of their duty; and survivorship benefits, primarily to the surviving legitimate spouse and dependent children.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2020-02-17

rows.author: B010
rows.title_full: AN ACT CODIFYING THE ALTERNATIVE CHILD CARE LAWS, REORGANIZING THE INTERCOUNTRY ADOPTION BOARD INTO THE NATIONAL AUTHORITY FOR CHILD CARE, AND PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract:
Creates a one stop shop on alternative child care attached to the DSWD whose functions shall include among others, the formulation and development of alternative child care policies such as but not limited to programs and services that will protect the Filipino child from abuse, exploitation, trafficking, and adoption practice that is harmful, detrimental and prejudicial to the best interest of the child.

Establishes a system of cooperation with other States, through their respective central or competent authorities and accredited bodies to prevent the sale, trafficking, and abduction of children, and to protect Filipino children abandoned overseas who are made vulnerable by their irregular status.

Incorporates provisions as regards to other forms of alternative child care options such as foster care, guardianship, kafalah care, kinship care, family-like care and residential care.
rows.status: Transmmitted to the Committee on Ways and Means on 2021-05-20

rows.author: I050
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING ALL MUNICIPAL MAYORS, CITY MAYORS AND PROVINCIAL GOVERNORS THE APPROPRIATE CIVIL SERVICE ELIGIBILITY, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Aims to recognize the immense amount of duties and responsibilities that these local government leaders have whose role is to incorporate the local development needs with national priorities to create holistic meso-level policies, programs and priorities for socio-economic growth.

Grants an eligibility to the former and current local government officials an equivalent of a Career Service Professional Eligibility who have served or who shall serve an aggregate period of nine (9) years in office, provided that they must be a holder of a bachelor's degree; while an eligibility of a Career Service Sub-Professional is hereby granted to those former and current officials who have served or who shall serve an aggregate period of six (6) years in office, provided that such officials shall have at least earned seventy-two (72) academic units leading to a bachelor's degree.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2020-02-17

rows.author: J092
rows.title_full: AN ACT MANDATING THE OVERSIGHT AND AUDIT OF GOVERNMENT INTELLIGENCE AND CONFIDENTIAL FUNDS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Defines \"intelligence funds\" as funds provided for those related to intelligence information gathering activities of uniformed and military personnel, and intelligence practitioners that have direct impact to national security; Also defines \"confidential funds\" as funds provided for those related to surveillance activities in civilian government agencies that are intended to support the mandate or operations of the agency.

States that confidential and intelligence funds shall be used for intelligence, counter-intelligence and confidential activities only upon the expressed recommendation of Congress via Joint Resolution, and the approval of the President of the Philippines.

Intends to fill the gaps of previous initiatives which does not fully address the issues concerning transparency, accountability and other malevolent issues surrounding the use of the funds, and therefore rectify the unconstitutional mode of allocating funds that are free from audit, public scrutiny and official accountability.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC ACCOUNTS since 2020-02-18

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING THE REVISED PENAL CODE'S ARTICLE 315 TO INCLUDE WILFUL NON-PAYMENT OF CORRECTLY IMPOSED PUBLIC TRANSPORTATION FEES AS A MODE OF COMMITTING ESTAFA
rows.abstract:
Aims to give protection to the drivers, riders and delivery men of common carriers or the new transportation methods such as Grab, Angkas, Lala Move, and Joy Ride.

Proposes therefore to amend the definition of Estafa or Swindling in order to prevent abuses of the new methods of engaging common-carriers who usually risk both their own funds and safety in delivering passengers and goods to their final destination.

Declares that any person who shall defraud another by \"willful refusal to pay the properly imposed fees to any common-carrier, regardless of the amount due\" shall be punished under Art.315 of Act No.3815 of the 
Revised Penal Code.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2020-02-18

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 6, CHAPTER II, TITLE II OF PRESIDENTIAL DECREE # 198, AS AMENDED
rows.abstract:
Provides that local officials have a compelling duty to address basic needs of their constituents, water being one of the most essential because they have a larger stake in the issue of water supply and sharper capacity because of the proximity to assess the problem than the central agency LWUA.

Provides that the autonomy of Metropolitan Cebu Water District (MCDW) and the other water districts in the country, which P.D.No.198 provides, shall not be interpreted to rule out oversight by LGUS in helping assure adequate supply of water to their constituents.

Amends therefore P.D.No.198, series of 1973 to allow and encourage the oversight by local governments on the performance of water districts.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2020-02-18

rows.author: H058
rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING A NATIONAL ORAL HEALTH PROGRAM AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract:
Seeks to strengthen the delivery of oral health services through the adoption of responsive and efficient policies in oral disease prevention and oral health promotion by scaling up essential programs and increasing investments to make oral health treatment and care more equitable and affordable for all Filipinos.

Proposes to establish a Program that will seek to improve the determinants of oral health; integrate oral health promotion and preventive services with the general health care system; and provide timely access to quality basic oral health care and treatment, among others.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2020-02-18

rows.title_full: AN ACT MANDATING THE CREATION OF AN EXTENDED PRODUCER RESPONSIBILITY SCHEME TO ADDRESS LEAKAGE OF PLASTIC WASTE INTO THE ENVIRONMENT, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Seeks to supplement RA9003 by addressing the problem of collection of plastic waste through the setting up of a system by which private companies that generate plastic will be responsible to collect an amount of plastic waste in proportion to the plastic generated by them, under the \"producer pays\" principle.

Defines several terms among others such as \"Producer Responsibility Organization (PRO) which is a legal entity that shall undertake resource recovery of plastic wastes on behalf of producers, founded voluntarily by companies and assumes responsibility for the take-back of the equivalent amount of plastic packaging they put into the market.
